timeline.title: Ten seats purchased
timeline.excerpt: Corporate card charge predates procurement intake by 17 days.

timeline.excerpt: Eight users authenticated before the request entered review.

timeline.title: Approval requested after launch
timeline.excerpt: We already bought ten seats. What does Security need so we can keep this moving?

timeline.title: Review request opened
timeline.excerpt: Request submitted after the team had begun using Nimbus for call coaching.

judgment.headline: Keep the coaching workflow. Contain the customer-data path.
judgment.hypothesis: The material issue is not Nimbus alone; Sales Enablement created a production data flow before anyone owned the boundary.
judgment.alternative: The enterprise retention control may already be enabled, which would narrow the immediate exposure but not repair the intake pattern.
judgment.recommendation: Verify the production tenant and transcript flow today, disable service-improvement retention if needed, and give Sales a bounded route to continue while CRM Platform becomes the technical owner.
tradeoffs: Makes the card-first intake pattern visible without punishing disclosure
conditions: Production connector owned by CRM Platform
judgment.changes_mind: If transcripts cannot be isolated from service-improvement use, suspend uploads until the tenant is corrected.

engagements.intended_use: Evaluate note quality using synthetic calls in an isolated lab tenant.

surface.summary: Enterprise retention can be disabled, but the setting must be verified per tenant.

team.name: CRM Platform
team.basis: The team arrives with a data boundary, measurements and a decision it needs.

timeline.title: Retention setting is tenant-specific
timeline.excerpt: Enterprise customers may disable service-improvement retention through an administrative setting.

timeline.title: CRM lab boundary
timeline.excerpt: Production connectors and copied customer records are prohibited in the evaluation tenant.

timeline.title: Decision framed with trade-offs
timeline.excerpt: We need a decision on whether the retention control is enough for a synthetic-only evaluation.

timeline.title: Evaluation requested before access
timeline.excerpt: The request defines a 30-day evaluation and prohibits production data.

timeline.title: Synthetic dataset prepared
timeline.excerpt: Evaluation corpus contains invented calls and generated contact records only.

timeline.title: Lab access granted
timeline.excerpt: OAuth grant followed the documented boundary review.

judgment.headline: Proceed with the lab evaluation.
judgment.hypothesis: CRM Platform has bounded the same Nimbus vendor fact through synthetic data, review-before-access and a documented lab boundary.
judgment.alternative: A copied production example could silently invalidate the boundary if the lab convention is not enforced.
judgment.recommendation: Continue the 30-day evaluation, name the exit owner and require a new decision before any production connector or customer record enters the tenant.
tradeoffs: Keeps customer data outside the evaluation
conditions: Production promotion requires a new review
missing: Named owner for access removal at day 30
judgment.changes_mind: Any production connector or customer record moves this engagement out of the lab boundary.

surface.summary: The published subprocessor notice changed after the recorded approval.

timeline.title: Production integration

timeline.title: Contract owner departed
timeline.excerpt: Evan Brooks left Finance Systems; no successor was recorded for LedgerLoop.

timeline.title: Renewal due
timeline.excerpt: Automatic renewal window closes in 21 days; contract owner remains Evan Brooks.

timeline.title: Notice term changed
timeline.excerpt: The published DPA replaced 30-day advance notice with notice through the online list.

judgment.headline: Put the changed term into the renewal already in flight.
judgment.hypothesis: A meaningful vendor term changed while the accountable owner field still points to someone who left, leaving a high-value production relationship unable to absorb drift.
judgment.alternative: LedgerLoop may still provide advance notice contractually even though the public wording changed.
judgment.recommendation: Assign the business owner now and extend CON-204 with the notice-term question; route any acceptance of online-only notice to the Controller before the renewal window closes.
tradeoffs: Keeps the production close workflow stable
Consumes negotiation time inside a 21-day window
conditions: Controller accepts or rejects the changed notice mechanism
missing: Whether the signed agreement preserves 30-day notice
judgment.changes_mind: A signed clause preserving advance notice would reduce this to an ownership correction.

heuristics.title: Assess the engagement, not the vendor in isolation

sections.use_when: A vendor finding is being treated as the decision.
sections.understand: The vendor surface is shared. Exposure, value, ownership and the team's way of working decide what the same fact means here.
sections.do: Attach the finding to a team, intended use and process before recommending action.
sections.uncertainty: The engagement may be incomplete even when the vendor evidence is strong.
sections.provenance: Normalized from the TPRM Lens product specification; awaiting separate public approval.

heuristics.title: Reconstruct sequence before calling it shadow IT

sections.use_when: Purchase, access, data use and intake dates are available.
sections.understand: Sequence distinguishes an early evaluation from a workflow already carrying customer data before review.
sections.do: Order the events and name exactly what preceded review.
sections.uncertainty: Missing identity or purchasing records can make a sequence look cleaner than it was.

heuristics.title: Contain the risky path without breaking the useful work

sections.use_when: A useful workflow is already running outside the review path.
sections.understand: A reflexive shutdown can move the behavior underground and destroy the relationship needed to correct it.
sections.do: Assess the live use, contain the material data path, verify the vendor control and give the team a route to continue safely.
sections.uncertainty: Immediate suspension remains appropriate when the material exposure cannot be bounded.
sections.provenance: Normalized from Pierre-Paul's TPRM intervention direction; proposed for public review.

heuristics.title: Read the same vendor fact through team maturity

sections.use_when: Two teams use the same vendor under different boundaries.
sections.understand: A team that arrives with boundaries and trade-offs needs a decision. A team that arrives after launch needs containment and a relationship intervention.
sections.do: Change the intervention, not the underlying vendor fact.
sections.uncertainty: Fluency is not maturity; ground the appraisal in prior exchanges.
sections.provenance: Adapted from the public Risk Lens maturity heuristic for TPRM; proposed.

heuristics.title: Refuse relationship judgment without history or intended use

sections.use_when: Fewer than two relevant interactions exist or intended use is unstated.
sections.understand: Vendor documentation cannot fill in what the business plans to send or how the team will operate the relationship.
sections.do: Abstain and ask only for the missing facts that change the decision. Do not call a model to invent maturity.
sections.uncertainty: Relevant history may exist in a source that was not connected.
sections.provenance: Adapted from the public Risk Lens abstention heuristic for TPRM; proposed.

heuristics.title: Treat vendor drift as a relationship event

sections.use_when: External terms or posture change after approval.
sections.understand: The changed sentence matters through the data flow, renewal window, owner and authority that can accept it.
sections.do: Reopen the affected engagement, name the changed trade-off and route it to the existing renewal work.
sections.uncertainty: A public wording change may only clarify an unchanged operational practice.
sections.provenance: Normalized from the Data Drift Detection and TPRM Lens specifications; proposed.

trace.label: Ten seats purchased
trace.detail: Corporate card charge predates procurement intake by 17 days.

trace.label: First Nimbus login
trace.detail: Eight users authenticated before the request entered review.

trace.label: Live transcripts enabled
trace.detail: Customer call transcripts were sent to the production Nimbus tenant.

trace.label: Approval requested after launch
trace.detail: We already bought ten seats. What does Security need so we can keep this moving?

trace.label: Review request opened
trace.detail: Request submitted after the team had begun using Nimbus for call coaching.

trace.label: Sales Enablement engages low
trace.detail: Prior reviews begin after purchase and ask Security to approve use already underway.

trace.label: Keep the coaching workflow. Contain the customer-data path.
trace.detail:
The material issue is not Nimbus alone; Sales Enablement created a production data flow before anyone owned the boundary.
Alternative: The enterprise retention control may already be enabled, which would narrow the immediate exposure but not repair the intake pattern.
Missing: Current production tenant retention setting

trace.label: investigate
trace.detail: Verify the production tenant and transcript flow today, disable service-improvement retention if needed, and give Sales a bounded route to continue while CRM Platform becomes the technical owner.

trace.detail: 2026-07-01 Retention setting is tenant-specific → 2026-07-10 CRM lab boundary → 2026-07-11 Decision framed with trade-offs → 2026-07-11 Evaluation requested before access → 2026-07-12 Synthetic dataset prepared → 2026-07-15 Lab access granted

trace.label: Retention setting is tenant-specific
trace.detail: Enterprise customers may disable service-improvement retention through an administrative setting.

trace.label: CRM lab boundary
trace.detail: Production connectors and copied customer records are prohibited in the evaluation tenant.

trace.label: Decision framed with trade-offs
trace.detail: We need a decision on whether the retention control is enough for a synthetic-only evaluation.

trace.label: Evaluation requested before access
trace.detail: The request defines a 30-day evaluation and prohibits production data.

trace.label: Synthetic dataset prepared
trace.detail: Evaluation corpus contains invented calls and generated contact records only.

trace.label: Lab access granted
trace.detail: OAuth grant followed the documented boundary review.

trace.label: CRM Platform engages high
trace.detail: The team arrives with a data boundary, measurements and a decision it needs.

trace.label: Proceed with the lab evaluation.
trace.detail:
CRM Platform has bounded the same Nimbus vendor fact through synthetic data, review-before-access and a documented lab boundary.
Alternative: A copied production example could silently invalidate the boundary if the lab convention is not enforced.
Missing: Named owner for access removal at day 30

trace.label: proceed with conditions
trace.detail: Continue the 30-day evaluation, name the exit owner and require a new decision before any production connector or customer record enters the tenant.
